records.title: Birth of Robert Douglas
records.text: Born May 8, 1876, at 9 Canon Street, Edinburgh. Father Archibald Douglas, wood merchant's traveller; mother Isabella Gray. Parents married 1863.

records.title: Birth of Agnes Brown, his mother
records.text: Born December 18, 1885, at Edston, Peebles. Father George Brown, ploughman; mother Christina Henderson.

records.title: Death of George Brown
records.text: April 5, 1886, Edston, Peebles. Ploughman, 23; son of William Brown and Agnes McGarth; husband of Christina Henderson.

records.title: Death of William Brown
records.text: January 13, 1895, The Harrow, Stobo. Ploughman, 59; husband of Agnes McGarth.

records.title: Marriage of Robert Douglas and Elizabeth Millar McDonald
records.text: June 9, 1899, 34 St Patrick Square, Edinburgh. He was a saw miller of 23; she a domestic servant, recorded as 24 (her birth date of May 31, 1874, would make her 25).

records.title: Marriage of James Lawson Parker
records.text: August 28, 1903, Coldstream, Carluke, Lanarkshire. Gamekeeper of Shieldhill, Biggar; son of Benjamin Parker, mason, and Jane Lawson, lady's maid. Bride Janet Crawford Stewart.

records.title: Birth of Lawrence Brown
records.text: June 14, 1907, 9 p.m., Royal Maternity Hospital, Edinburgh. Father's column blank. Mother Agnes Brown, domestic servant, domicile Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar.

records.title: Census: Laurence B. Douglas, age 3
records.text: 16 Lochrin Place, Edinburgh. Recorded as Laurence B., son, 3, in the household with Elizabeth Douglas, wife, and Janet, daughter, 10. The household entry continues across pages.

records.title: Census: James Parker at Shieldhill Mains
records.text: 3 Shieldhill Mains, Libberton. Gamekeeper, 38, born Biggar, with his wife Janet and children John, Euphemia and Robert. Gean Tree Cottage is on the same page.

records.title: Marriage of Agnes McGarth Brown
records.text: August 28, 1911, Edinburgh, to Thomas McKay McKenzie, asylum attendant. She was an asylum nurse at West House.

records.title: Birth of Mary Christina McKenzie
records.text: May 6, 1912, 9 Stewart Terrace, Edinburgh. Daughter of Thomas McKay McKenzie and Agnes Brown.

records.title: Thomas McKenzie enlists
records.text: Names his wife, Agnes, born Brown, and their daughters Mary (1912) and Jean (1914).
records.ref: British Army WWI service record, Thomas McKenzie

records.title: Death of Robert Douglas
records.text: September 9, 1919, Woodburn Sanatorium, Edinburgh, age 43. Pulmonary tuberculosis. Home 5 Foundry Street, Dunfermline.

records.title: Census: Lawrence Douglas, age 14
records.text: 5 Foundry Street, Dunfermline. Message boy for a grocer. Elizabeth a widow and school cleaner; Janet a clerkess.

records.title: Sails on the Duchess of Bedford
records.text: September 7, 1929, from Greenock. Lawrence Brown, 22, grocer, travelling with his sister Janet Crombie.
records.ref: Passenger manifest, S.S. Duchess of Bedford, list D

records.title: Arrives in Canada
records.text: September 13, 1929. Names his mother, Mrs. Elizabeth Anderson, 39 Grieve Street, Dunfermline, and his brother-in-law Thomas Crombie of Chicago.

records.title: Enters the United States at Detroit
records.text: September 15, 1929. Lawrence Brown, 22, grocer, born Edinburgh, bound for Chicago.
records.ref: Detroit arrival manifest, Form 548, M1478, roll 8

records.title: Leaves Greenock
records.text: September 7, 1929, aboard the Duchess of Bedford. Laurence Brown, 22, grocer, 39 Grieve Street, Dunfermline.
records.ref: UK outward passenger list, Duchess of Bedford

records.title: Census: Lawrence Brown in Chicago
records.text: April 14, 1930. Brother-in-law in the Crombie household; salesman, grocery.

records.title: Elizabeth Anderson comes to America
records.text: October 2, 1934, Port Huron, Michigan. Elizabeth Anderson, 60, born Edinburgh, joining her daughter, Mrs. Janet Crombie, 1518 Kostner Avenue, Chicago.
records.ref: Form I-448, port of Port Huron, M1478

records.title: Providence directory: display manager
records.text: Lawrence Douglas, display manager, 165 Weybosset Street; rooms at 35 Elmwood Avenue.

records.title: Providence directory: display manager
records.text: Lawrence Douglas, display manager, 165 Weybosset Street; rooms at 459 Pine Street.

records.title: Marriage to Constance Darcy
records.text: October 9, 1939, Birmingham, Alabama. Lawrence Douglas, 32, salesman, and Constance Darcy, 26, of Providence.
records.ref: Jefferson County Marriage License Record, book 154, p. 409

records.title: Census: San Francisco
records.text: April 11, 1940. Laurence Douglas, 32, window trimmer, retail clothing; with his wife, Constance.

records.title: Draft registration
records.text: October 16, 1940, San Francisco. Laurence Brown Douglas, 129 Julian Avenue; Bond Stores Inc.

records.title: Re-enters the U.S. at Blaine
records.text: June 21, 1941, Blaine, Washington. Lawrence Brown Douglas, 33, display man, with his wife, Constance.

records.title: Albert Darcy registers for the draft
records.text: Albert Blake Darcy, 53, born Rumford, R.I., 1888; 60 Blake Street, Shawomet; Providence Journal.
records.ref: WWII draft card, R.I., serial U-40

records.title: Petition for naturalization
records.text: Signed Laurence Brown Douglas. Gives his entry at Detroit, September 15, 1929, under the name Lawrence Brown.

records.title: Becomes a U.S. citizen
records.text: May 6, 1943, Pittsburgh. Oath of allegiance signed Laurence Brown Douglas; certificate no. 5862979.

records.title: Pawtucket directory: 97 Magill Street
records.text: Laurence B. Douglas (Constance E.), window dresser, house at 97 Magill Street.

records.title: Providence directory: 148 General Street
records.text: Lawrence B. Douglas and his wife Constance, house at 148 General Street.

records.title: Providence directory: Carter's Men Store
records.text: Laurence B. Douglas (Constance E.), displayman, Carter's Men Store, Pawtucket; 644 River Avenue.

records.title: Obituary
records.text: Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, page 3. Died in St. Joseph’s Hospital, Providence; of 644 River Avenue.

records.title: Providence directory: his own business
records.text: Laurence B. Douglas (Constance E.), window displays, 644 River Avenue.

people.name: Laurence Brown Douglas
people.text: Born Lawrence Brown in Edinburgh. Raised as a Douglas in Edinburgh and Dunfermline. Grocer, then window trimmer and display man in Chicago, Providence, San Francisco and Pawtucket. Became a U.S. citizen in Pittsburgh in 1943.

people.name: Agnes McGarth Brown
people.text: His mother. A servant from Upper Clydesdale who lived at Gean Cottage, Shieldhill. Later an asylum nurse; married Thomas McKenzie in 1911 and had two daughters, Mary and Jean.

people.name: Robert Douglas
people.text: The man who raised him. Saw miller, then stone machineman. Died of tuberculosis when Laurence was twelve.

people.name: Elizabeth Millar McDonald
people.text: Lizzie Douglas, later Elizabeth Anderson. The woman who raised him, and the one he always named as his mother.

people.name: Janet Page Douglas Crombie
people.text: His sister in the Douglas household. Sailed with him to America in 1929; lived in Chicago.

people.name: Constance Eugenie Darcy
people.text: His wife from 1939. A nurse. Buried with him at Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston.

people.name: Mary Archibald
people.text: Sewing mistress at Gean Tree, Quothquan, a few doors from the Hendersons. In 1901 she lived alone at Gean Tree.

people.name: Alexander Archibald
people.text: Mary's brother. Domestic gardener at Shieldhill House in 1901.

people.name: James Lawson Parker
people.text: Raised as an 'adopted son' in the Henderson household where Agnes grew up. Recorded as a gamekeeper living at Shieldhill in 1903 and at Shieldhill Mains in 1911, married with three children.

people.name: Andrew Henderson
people.text: Agnes's uncle, a groom, head of Lime Tree Cottage in 1901. Remembered in the village as a poet and beekeeper.

people.name: Sir Nathaniel Dunlop
people.text: Glasgow shipowner who bought Shieldhill in 1898. Knighted July 1907, weeks after Laurence's birth; honorary Doctor of Laws.

timeline: Born Lawrence Brown at the Royal Maternity Hospital, Lauriston Place, Edinburgh.
The King's birthday honours name Nathaniel Dunlop, owner of Shieldhill, for a knighthood.
July 4, 1907
Birth registered by his mother, Agnes Brown, at 24 Forrest Road.
Dunlop knighted at Buckingham Palace; the Gazette of July 26 gives his address as Shieldhill, Biggar.
April 2, 1911
Census: Laurence B. Douglas, 3, "son," at 16 Lochrin Place, Edinburgh, with Elizabeth Douglas and her daughter Janet.
August 19, 1912
Admitted to Queen Anne Infant School, Dunfermline, Fife, as Lawrence Douglas; the register calls him "Adopted" and names his guardian.
January 11, 1916
Transfers to Queen Anne Primary, entry 1191; the register gives his guardian, Robert Douglas, at 5 Foundry Street, Dunfermline.
Zeppelin raid on Leith and Edinburgh; a bomb falls on Lauriston Place, the same street as his birthplace.
September 9, 1919
Robert Douglas, who raised him, dies of tuberculosis at Woodburn Sanatorium, Edinburgh, aged 43.
October 8, 1920
Leaves school at thirteen, "Granted Exemption by E.A."
Census: Lawrence Douglas, 14, message boy for a grocer, at 5 Foundry Street, Dunfermline; Elizabeth Douglas a widow.
His sister Janet marries Thomas Crombie; she enters the U.S. at Detroit, September 13, 1926.
September 7, 1929
Sails from Greenock on the Duchess of Bedford with Janet.
September 13, 1929
Arrives at Quebec on the Duchess of Bedford.
September 15, 1929
Enters the United States at Detroit as Lawrence Brown, age 22.
October 2, 1934
Elizabeth Douglas, now Mrs. Elizabeth Anderson, enters the United States at Port Huron, Michigan, to live with Janet in Chicago.
Providence directories list a Lawrence Douglas, display manager, 165 Weybosset Street.
September 21, 1938
The Great Hurricane floods downtown Providence.
October 9, 1939
Marries Constance Eugenie Darcy in Birmingham, Alabama.
Window trimmer and displayman for Bond Stores, San Francisco.
February 11, 1943
Petitions for naturalization in Pittsburgh as Laurence Brown Douglas.
Takes the oath and is admitted a citizen of the United States, Pittsburgh.
Window dresser, 97 Magill Street, Pawtucket.
Display worker, 148 General Street, Providence.
Display work, 644 River Avenue, Providence; displayman at Carter's Men Store, Pawtucket, in 1960.
March 9, 1961
Dies at St. Joseph's Hospital, Providence, age 53.
March 13, 1961
Funeral announced from the Ruth E. Urquhart funeral home, Warwick; burial at Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston.
places: Royal Maternity Hospital, 79 Lauriston Place, Edinburgh

1534 South Kostner Avenue, Chicago (1929 manifest and border card; the 1930 census reads 1532)
Valencia Street, San Francisco (1940 census; no house number given)
612 California Avenue, Avalon, Pennsylvania (Pittsburgh district from about September 1941)
